reconstructed_statement.carrier: For every natural m,n and every A in real m-by-n matrices, put r=min(m,n).
reconstructed_statement.output: One specified returned pair R in real m-by-r and Q in real r-by-n, with A=RQ and QQ^T=I_r.
reconstructed_statement.definition_kind: Literal deterministic construction from a specified exact-real adjacent elimination procedure in the wide branch, and the literal pair (A,I_n) in the tall branch; not choice of arbitrary factors satisfying a characterization.
reconstructed_statement.rank: r is the minimum shape dimension, not rank(A). Zero/dependent rows are included. Q is an orthonormal row frame even when coefficients in R vanish.
reconstructed_statement.scalar_transpose: Real field with ordinary transpose, not conjugate transpose over a complex extension.
reconstructed_statement.quantum_slots: No register/basis order, oracle, ancilla, phase quotient, success probability, approximation tolerance or quantum circuit is part of this matrix theorem. These are not silently inherited from downstream uses.

source_nodes.content: The record obligation is exactly A=RQ and QQ^T=I_min(m,n). Merely defining the record does not produce factors.

source_nodes.anchor: The fixed row elimination procedure, rho and alpha definitions
source_nodes.content: rho=sqrt(x^2+y^2). At rho=0 use alpha=0. Otherwise alpha is negative arccos(x/rho) for y<0, positive arccos(x/rho) for y>=0.
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: Squares are nonnegative, so rho=0 implies x=y=0. Otherwise rho>0 and |x|<=rho. For u=x/rho, sin(arccos u)=sqrt(1-u^2)=|y|/rho. Negating precisely when y<0 gives sin(alpha)=y/rho; cosine stays x/rho.

source_nodes.anchor: Half-angle plane matrix and zero-pair paragraph
source_nodes.content: theta=-2 alpha, ordered rows top/bottom, plane [[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]].
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: At theta=-2alpha this is [[c,s],[-s,c]]. Multiplying (x,y)^T gives ((x^2+y^2)/rho,(-yx+xy)/rho)^T=(rho,0)^T when rho>0. The zero branch is identity and sends (0,0) to itself. c^2+s^2=1 gives orthogonality and determinant one. Left multiplication updates both entire rows, not isolated pivot entries.

source_nodes.anchor: For a matrix B with N rows and M columns
source_nodes.content: Columns c=0,...,M-1 are processed in order. If c<N, adjacent ordered pairs descend from (N-2,N-1) to (c,c+1). Each angle uses the current evolving matrix. If c>=N, no pair is processed. Empty pair ranges do nothing.

source_nodes.anchor: Bottom-up pass and induction over columns
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: Within a column, rotations eliminate from the bottom upward; later pairs do not touch already eliminated lower rows. For an earlier column i<c, both affected row indices are at least c, hence both entries were already zero. A plane rotation preserves this zero pair. Column induction therefore gives T(B)_{ji}=0 for every i<j, with no full-rank premise.

source_nodes.anchor: S(B), T(B) and chronological list equations
source_nodes.content: For chronological rotations G_1,...,G_s, S=G_s...G_1 and T=SB. Products of orthogonal planes give S^T S=I_N.
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: The first matrix acts first on B, so successive left multiplication puts the newest rotation on the left. Multiplication of plane orthogonality identities cancels factors in S^T S.

source_nodes.anchor: Consequently S(B)^T T(B)=B and square orthogonality paragraph
source_nodes.content: S^T T=S^T S B=B. Since S is square in finite dimension, S^T S=I also gives S S^T=I.
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: A square matrix with a left inverse is invertible, so the left inverse is also its right inverse. This second orientation, not just S^T S, supplies the row inner products used below.

source_nodes.content: For m<=n, eliminate B=A^T of shape n-by-m. Define R_ik=T(B)_ki for i,k<m; Q_kj=S(B)_kj for k<m,j<n. These are actual residual/transform prefix entries from that one procedure.

source_nodes.anchor: Transposed recovery, full sum, tail removal and prefix-sum paragraph
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: Transpose S^T T=A^T to obtain T^T S=A. Thus A_ij=sum_{ell<n} T_{ell,i} S_{ell,j}. For ell>=m and i<m, i<ell, so the residual invariant kills T_{ell,i}. The remaining ell<m terms are exactly sum_k R_ik Q_kj. This is prefix removal of proven zero terms, not rank truncation or an approximation.

source_nodes.anchor: Leading transform rows and inner-product equation
source_nodes.reconstructed_proof: For a,b<m, QQ^T entry is sum_{j<n} S_aj S_bj=(SS^T)_ab=delta_ab. Taking a prefix of orthonormal rows preserves the same pairwise inner products. Combined with wide reconstruction this supplies both record obligations.

source_nodes.anchor: Tall and empty matrices, dimension comparison
source_nodes.content: If m<=n, return the wide pair with r=m. If m>n, return R=A and Q=I_n with r=n. The latter branch has A=AI_n and I_n I_n^T=I_n but no triangularity guarantee. Dimension comparison fixes the branch; no existence theorem selects the output.

At m=0 the wide branch has an empty inner dimension and no columns to eliminate. At n=0<m, use the tall empty identity. At m=n=0 use wide. Matrix identities and sums have empty indexing sets; I_0 is an empty matrix, not a scalar 1.

boundary_discriminators.negative_y: For x=0,y=-1, alpha=-pi/2 and theta=pi. The half-angle plane [[0,-1],[1,0]] sends (0,-1) to (1,0), fixing both the signed angle and negative-two multiplier convention.
boundary_discriminators.negative_x_zero_y: For x=-1,y=0, the y>=0 branch uses alpha=pi, theta=-2pi and the plane is -I_2 on the pair, sending (-1,0) to (1,0). No negative-pivot exclusion is permitted.
boundary_discriminators.zero_pair: For x=y=0 the entire selected rows still undergo the specified identity operation. It is not a fabricated zero matrix or arbitrary angle after division by zero.
boundary_discriminators.rank_zero: If A=0, all pivot pairs are zero, S is identity, Q is its first m rows in the wide case and R=0; in the tall case Q=I_n,R=0. This provides orthonormal Q without nonzero input rows.
boundary_discriminators.rank_deficiency: Repeated rows do not change the retained inner dimension and do not invalidate zero-tail removal. R may be singular or zero; Q remains a row frame.
boundary_discriminators.square_boundary: m=n belongs to the wide branch, not tall. Correctness does not require that every final diagonal entry be positive, because a last-row singleton has no pair to rotate.
boundary_discriminators.wide_extreme: For m=1,n>1, bottom-up elimination of the one column of A^T produces an n-row transform; only its first row is retained in Q.
boundary_discriminators.tall_extreme: For m>n=1, R=A and Q=[1]; no elimination or triangularity assertion is needed.
boundary_discriminators.empty_extremes: m=0,n>0 yields empty R,Q with r=0; n=0<m uses empty identity; m=n=0 uses wide. All displayed identities have correctly empty carriers.
